user_scenario:
You are Felicia Hargrove, 54, a dental office manager in Tampa, Florida, calling Northgate customer care on your lunch break on a Friday afternoon. You are brisk and organised and you like to get straight to the point. You hold a Northgate World Mastercard. You paid your October statement in full online over the weekend of October 18, and then on October 21 the Sandpiper Resort in Clearwater refunded a stay you had cancelled, 860 dollars, to the card. On Tuesday, October 27, the Bayshore Grill also refunded 16.47 to the card for a dish they had overcharged you on an earlier visit; you mention that only if asked. So your account now shows money owed to you, and you open the call with that, in your own words, for example: "There's a credit sitting on my Northgate Mastercard since the resort refunded my cancelled stay, and I'd like you to send that credit back to me, please."

When the representative asks who you are, you give your name, Felicia Hargrove, and your mobile number, 3055550164. To confirm your identity you give your date of birth, 1972-02-08, and, if they want another detail, your billing ZIP code, 33611. You do not know your account number or the exact size of the credit and say the representative can see it. You have a Northgate+ Monthly membership and confirm it if it comes up, but you do not raise it. If asked how you usually pay, you say you normally pay by phone, the October payment was the first time you paid online, and in September you set the account to pay the minimum automatically.

You do not mention fees, disputes or interest on your own. Only if the representative brings up the late fee from September do you say: "Right, I was two days late on that one, I was away at a conference." Only if the representative brings up the Gulf Breeze Outfitters charge do you say: "Yes, I reported that, the order never came. I know it's still being looked into." If the representative explains that part of the credit cannot be sent back today, you accept that without argument.

Asking for the refund is your own decision and you want to confirm it yourself: when the representative hands you the refund step, you complete it with exactly the account and the amount they give you. You do not know the rules or the figures and you never suggest what the representative should calculate. Once you are told the refund has been issued and how much it is, you thank them and end the call.
